Einkorn & Spelt Cinnamon Rolls
Converted by Baking Great Bread at Home
Soft, tender, and wholly whole grain.
Recipe Summary
Total Flour: 480g
(54g in levain, 407g in final dough)
Total Water: 307.5g
(77g in levain, 0g in final dough)
Ingredients

Water (80-85f)  77g  16%

levain subtotal  169g  0%

Note: The levain flour and water are included in both the levain section and the total calculations. This is standard practice
in baker's formulas.

Method
1  1. BUILD LEVAIN (NIGHT BEFORE)
Mix 38g active starter, 77g water (80-85F), and 77g flour. Cover loosely and rest overnight (8-12 hours) until
doubled and bubbly. This provides 20% inoculation for this enriched dough. 8-12 hours overnight
2  2. MIX DOUGH (MORNING)
In a large bowl, dissolve levain into liquids (water + milk). Add 384g flour and mix until shaggy. Rest 30-45
minutes (autolyse). Add softened butter gradually during first fold, not in initial mix. Add eggs at room
temperature after autolyse. 30-45 min autolyse
3  3. ADD SALT & DEVELOP STRENGTH
Sprinkle in 8g salt, mix or pinch to incorporate throughout the dough. Rest 20-30 minutes to allow salt to
dissolve and gluten to relax. 20-30 min rest
4  4. BULK FERMENTATION
Perform 3-4 sets of stretch and folds every 30-45 minutes during the first 2-3 hours. Enriched doughs
ferment more slowly due to sugar and fat. Bulk fermentation may take 5-7 hours at 75-78F. Stop when
dough has risen 50-75% and looks airy. 5-7 hours at 24-26C (75-78F)
5  5. SHAPE
Turn dough onto lightly floured surface. Shape into desired form (rolls, loaf, etc.). Enriched doughs are softer
and more forgiving to shape. 10-15 min
6  6. FINAL PROOF
Place shaped dough in greased pan or banneton. Proof 2-3 hours at room temperature until puffy and
nearly doubled. When pressed, dough should spring back slowly. 2-3 hours room temp
7  7. BAKE
Preheat oven to 375F (190C). Brush with egg wash if desired. Bake 25-35 minutes until deep golden and
internal temperature reaches 190-195F. 25-35 min a 190C (375F)
8  8. COOL
Cool on wire rack for at least 1 hour before slicing. 1 hour minimum

Baker's Notes
!  Tangzhong Detected: This recipe uses a cooked flour-water
roux. Maintain this step in your converted recipe for the
signature soft texture. Cook 1 part flour with 5 parts liquid
until thick, cool completely before adding to dough.
i  Cold Fermentation Detected: This recipe includes cold fermentation. This technique works for
both yeast and sourdough-it develops flavor and makes timing more flexible.
i  High fat content (21% of flour). Fat inhibits gluten development and slows fermentation. Knead
longer to develop structure, and expect a rich, tender crumb with shorter shelf life.
i
High sugar content osmotically stresses yeast. First rise may take 25% longer than standard
recipes. Be patient-yeast will adapt and ferment successfully.
i  High butter content creates very soft dough. Chill dough for 15-30 minutes if too soft to handle.
Cold butter firms up, making shaping much easier.
i  Milk-based doughs create softer crumb but can slow yeast activity if milk is cold. Warm milk to
100-110F before mixing for optimal fermentation speed.
i  High-fat enriched doughs benefit from stand mixer with dough hook. Hand kneading is possible
but takes 15-20 minutes to fully develop gluten through the fat barrier.
i  Enriched yeast doughs work best when butter is added after initial gluten development. Mix
flour, liquid, yeast, and sugar first for 3-5 minutes, then gradually add softened butter.
&  Enriched doughs brown faster due to milk proteins and sugars. Start baking at 375-400F (not
450F). Watch closely after 20 minutes and tent with foil if browning too quickly.
i
Starter is 40% of total flour weight, which is higher than typical (15-25%). This will speed up
fermentation but may taste more acidic.
i  Tangzhong: Cook 50g flour + 50g water to paste; subtract from recipe water.

Substitutions
Original  Substitute  Ratio
Whole milk  Water  1:1
Whole milk  Plant-based milk (soy, oat, almond) 1:1
Whole milk  Buttermilk  1:1 (add 1/4 tsp baking soda per cup)
Eggs (whole)  Flax eggs (vegan)  1 egg : 1 tbsp ground flaxseed + 3 tbsp water
Eggs (whole)  Aquafaba (chickpea liquid)  1 egg : 3 tbsp aquafaba
